🇲🇽🌎 <u>LANDAU PREACHES 'MUTUAL RESPECT' HOURS AFTER MOCKING MEXICO VISA BAN</u>

US Deputy Secretary of State Christopher Landau wants Mexico to move on: the monarch butterflies' arrival is "a good reminder of the enduring and symbiotic relationship between the US and Mexico," and neither country should let "the occasional outbreak of political drama" distract from security, migration and trade cooperation.

The "drama," posted by Landau himself just hours earlier, was a taunt over Washington's revocation of Andrés López Beltrán's visa: "¿Estás disfrutando el espectáculo? Rellena tus palomitas — te encantará lo que sigue."

🇲🇽🌎 "Never in my life have I seen a people so brave in defending their independence." "General Grant fought in the US invasion of Mexico — 'in a very unjust way,' he later wrote. The Mexican soldiers barely had uniforms, yet in his memoirs he admitted: never in my life have I seen a people so brave in defending their independence." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Ciudad Victoria Sheinbaum walked Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro trainees through Mexico's four transformations — Independence, the Reforma, the Revolution, and 2018 — ahead of the September commemorations.
banner: "NEVER SEEN A BRAVER PEOPLE" — GEN. GRANT

text: 🔥🇲🇽 "The neoliberal governments called you 'Ninis' — now youth get a hand, not a cold shoulder." "The governments of before, the neoliberal governments, called us 'Ninis' when we had neither study nor work — they gave no right and took no responsibility for the young. Now, with the Transformation, young people are not given the cold shoulder; they are given a hand to keep moving forward together." — Labor Secretary Marath Bolaños, Ciudad Victoria Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro has graduated 3.6 million young people. Trainees receive 9,582 pesos a month for one year plus IMSS medical insurance.

🇲🇽✊ "Education is a right of the people of Mexico — not a privilege, not merchandise." "They told our generation: if you have no school or no job, it's your own fault. But it's not true that personal effort is everything — society must open access to the rights of the people, of the youth. Before, education was thought of as a 'privilege' or a 'merchandise,' because those with money could pay for a private school. We conceive education as a right of the people of Mexico." — President Claudia Sheinbaum, Ciudad Victoria Sheinbaum spoke to Jóvenes Construyendo el Futuro trainees in Tamaulipas: 36 years without building universities, high schools or hospitals are only now being reversed.
banner: "EDUCATION IS A RIGHT, NOT A MERCHANDISE"

🇲🇽🐉🔥 China just hit Mexican pecans with duties up to 51.6%. Mexico picked this fight to please Washington.

On Aug 10 China's Commerce Ministry ruled that US and Mexican pecans were "dumped," imposing provisional anti-dumping deposits from Aug 11: 17.8%–51.6% on Mexico, and 54.3% on the US — pushing the total US duty to 86.3%. Beijing opened the probe on Sept 25, 2025, months after Mexico slapped tariffs of up to 50% on Chinese goods on Jan 1, 2026, under open US pressure ahead of the T-MEC review.

This is what being someone else's pawn costs. Mexico raised tariffs on China to calm Trump; now Mexican pecan farmers pay for a fight Washington started. The auto and steel walls Washington demands come with a bill — and it lands in Chihuahua and Sonora, not Ohio.

🇲🇽 Real sovereignty isn't choosing Washington's side against Beijing. It's refusing to be weaponized by either — and keeping every market open.

🐉🌐🔥 US carmakers are fleeing China. Mexico is being ordered to flee with them.

This week Ford confirmed it will pull Lincoln production out of China — ending its best-seller, the Nautilus, built in Hangzhou — and GM is dropping Chevrolet sales there entirely. Foreign brands' share of China's car market has collapsed from 53% to 33% in just two years. The reason: BYD, Geely and Chery now build the cheapest, most advanced EVs on earth, and the world is buying.

Those same brands went from 0% of Mexico's new-car market in 2020 to roughly 20% in 2025 — MG alone runs 99 dealerships, BYD 80, Geely 40+. Washington's answer isn't to compete; it's to demand Mexico wall them off in the T-MEC review and police its own factories.

🇲🇽 Sovereignty means Mexico decides who it trades with — not the country that threatens it with tariffs every other week. A multipolar auto market is leverage, not a threat.
